page: Microsoft Azure E128pds_v7 belongs to the memory-optimized Epdsv7 family and is deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The virtual machine delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs operating on the 64-bit ARM (arm64) instruction set architecture. It provides 1024 GB of total system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are not included, resulting in a GPU count of zero.

Integrated local storage is bundled directly with the instance, providing 7560 GB of NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Premium Storage. This local volume provides low-latency capacity for high-throughput read and write operations. Because the system relies on the arm64 architecture, application stacks must support ARM environments, and x86-specific instruction extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are unavailable. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are allocated by default.

The deployment of ARM-based hardware provides high resource density across memory and storage tiers. The balanced combination of 1024 GB of memory and high-capacity NVMe SSD storage accommodates intensive data manipulation without requiring distributed node overhead. Microsoft Azure E128pds_v7 is suitable for large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, distributed caching layers, and high-volume data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E128pds_v7 is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine delivered via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates 128 dedicated vCPUs paired with 1024 GB of RAM, establishing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It integrates 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage options, though it does not include GPU accelerators or default complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Lacking x86 extensions like AVX or AMX, execution relies on ARM instruction sets. The high resource density of compute cores, multi-terabyte NVMe storage, and substantial memory capacity enables efficient scaling for resource-intensive enterprise operations. Microsoft Azure E128pds_v7 is structured for workloads such as large in-memory databases, distributed key-value caches, analytical data processing pipelines, and enterprise database hosting requiring high memory capacity and fast local I/O.
